subject: P0 — Westshore AZ3 5xx surge: rapid redispatch and exec update
messages:
From: Natalie Cortez <natalie.cortez@westshore-pay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: James Harper <james.harper@westshore-pay.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High 5xx spike impacting transaction pipeline (AZ3)

SoojIN — we’re seeing a sudden surge of 5xx errors from requests routed to AZ3 starting ~09:05 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 18% in ~6 minutes and total TPS dropped by ~60%. We’ve pulled traces and attached a cropped set of request ids (westshore-logs-0601.zip).

This is impacting checkout storefronts in the west region. Can you confirm whether this is a regional problem on your side or a routing flap? Our NOC is standing by; we need either an immediate mitigation or a plan to redirect traffic off AZ3.

Cc’ing our CTO James for visibility.

—Natalie
Ops Lead, Westshore Payments
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Cortez <natalie.cortez@westshore-pay.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx spike impacting transaction pipeline (AZ3)

Thanks Natalie — picking this up.

Quick summary from logs: 5xx surface across the model-serving tier (seq_len spikes + KV cache misses) and an increase in connection resets from a subset of AZ3 boxes. I’m asking infra to assess capacity and routing so we can either heal AZ3 quickly or divert traffic. Marissa, Rishi — please confirm if we have an immediate cross-region reroute we can activate (preferably to us-west-2) and whether we need a warm pool to avoid cold-cache latency cliffs.

Action items:
- Rishi: snapshot current node health, isolate failing instance set, and confirm capacity in us-west-2.
- Marissa: prep a temporary routing policy (force-pref: us-west-2 for Westshore) and a rollback plan.
- Sean: prep customer comms and exec note.

I’ll coordinate with Natalie while we move.

—SoojIN
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Cortez <natalie.cortez@westshore-pay.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx spike impacting transaction pipeline (AZ3)

Confirming — I’m drafting a routing override now.

Planned steps (t=0+):
1) Enable emergency route preference: Westshore -> us-west-2 (gradual 10% ramps over 2m windows) to avoid immediate cache stampede. (reroute-policy-v2.json attached)
2) Isolate suspect AZ3 hosts from LB pool (Rishi to provide host list).
3) Spin up 10% warm instances in us-west-2 with cached prefixes for the high-frequency endpoints (prefix list derived from attached logs).
4) If error rate <2% after 8m, continue ramp to full; else trigger rollback and fall back to dedicated minimal-capacity nodes.

Attachment: reroute-policy-v2.json (policy, ramping schedule)

I’ll execute once infra confirms the host drain is safe.

—Marissa
Director, Incident Response
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Cortez <natalie.cortez@westshore-pay.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx spike impacting transaction pipeline (AZ3)

On Thu, Jun 1, 2028 at 09:26, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Confirming — I’m drafting a routing override now.

We’ve identified a partial network fabric degradation affecting AZ3 egress to the storage tier which is increasing KV cache miss latencies and causing cascading request timeouts. Isolation complete for 6/24 suspect instances (IDs: i-0a1b2c3d, i-0e4f5g6h, ...).

Capacity check: us-west-2 has spare capacity to absorb ~70% of AZ3 baseline traffic immediately; we’ll warm a 12-node pool seeded with most-used prefix keys. Warm pool will take ~6–9 minutes to reach steady-state depending on prefix lengths.

I’m green to start Marissa’s ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Starting host drain and init warm pool now. I’ll post updates on progress and any abnormal latencies during the ramp.

—Rishi
VP, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Natalie Cortez <natalie.cortez@westshore-pay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx spike impacting transaction pipeline (AZ3)

Thanks team — I can confirm our checkout error rate dropped to ~1.9% after the first ramp to 40% traffic shift, but we’re seeing a spike in tail latency for a subset of tokenization-heavy requests (p95 increased from 120ms -> 620ms). Customers are still reporting slow page loads for some flows. Any estimated time until warm pool caches the heavy prefixes?

Also, we have an internal postmortem form we’d like filled for our SRE review — will you be sharing a timeline and root cause once stabilized?

—Natalie
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: James Harper <james.harper@westshore-pay.com>, Natalie Cortez <natalie.cortez@westshore-pay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: P0 — Westshore AZ3 5xx surge: rapid redispatch and exec update

Executive summary (for James / Westshore execs):
- Incident start: 09:05 PDT — sudden network fabric degradation in AZ3 increased KV-cache miss latencies and connection resets, propagating to 5xxs.
- Mitigation: emergency routing override to us-west-2 initiated at 09:26 PDT with gradual ramping (10% -> 40% successful).
- Impact: peak 5xx rate ~18% at ~09:12; reduced to ~1.9% after initial ramps. Tail latency p95 increased for tokenization-heavy endpoints during warm-up. Estimated warm pool steady state: 6–9 minutes after warm node provisioning.
- Current status: traffic at ~60% shifted; error rates nominal; working through tail latency.
- Next steps: Rishi to finalize host remediation in AZ3, Marissa to publish rollback/route removal play, Sean to circulate a short customer-facing timeline and a draft postmortem (attached: postmortem-draft.md).

We’ll share a complete timeline and RCA once AZ3 is healthy and we’ve validated recovery. Appreciate the patience and the quick help from the Redwood infra/IR teams.

—SoojIN
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md
